story_type: spacecraft deliberately rams an asteroid, live onboard camera
hook: NASA flew this spacecraft into an asteroid. On purpose.
narration: NASA flew this spacecraft straight into an asteroid. On purpose.
The target was Dimorphos, a small moon just five hundred thirty feet across, circling a bigger asteroid about seven million miles from Earth.
Neither asteroid was a threat. This was the first planetary defense test, a real try at knocking a space rock off course.
After ten months in space, the spacecraft, called DART, closed in at roughly fourteen thousand miles an hour.
Its camera kept sending pictures home, and the little moon grew from a dot into a world of boulders.
Astronomers on Earth would judge the hit by timing how long Dimorphos took to loop around its partner.
[short pause] Then the pictures stopped, and the control room erupted.
outcome: The crash shortened Dimorphos's orbit around its partner asteroid by thirty two minutes.
title: Ramming an asteroid at 14,000 mph
description:
On Sept. 26, 2022, NASA's DART spacecraft deliberately crashed into the small asteroid moon Dimorphos at roughly 14,000 mph in the first planetary defense test. The impact shortened Dimorphos's orbit by 32 minutes.
